Close button audit

The round ✕ appears in 47 places: 24 bottom sheets (iOS only) and 23 centered pop-ups (both platforms). Your instinct is right. Neither Apple nor Material puts an ✕ on these surfaces, so the recommendation is to remove it everywhere and give the few pop-ups that need a way out a plain "Cancel" button.

The rule, from the platform guidelines
  1. Bottom sheets: no ✕. On iOS, a sheet that stops partway up the screen (Maps, Find My, Wallet) closes with the grabber, a swipe down, or a tap above it. Apple's Human Interface Guidelines ask for a Cancel or Done button only when the sheet is a full-height task with something to lose. Material 3 bottom sheets never draw an ✕, and Android here already has none. Ours are all short, and every one already closes on swipe, tap outside and Back.
  2. Centered pop-ups: never an ✕. Apple alerts and Material dialogs dismiss with a text button ("Cancel", "Keep editing"), not a corner icon. A confirm needs a Cancel next to its action. A picker that applies the moment you tap an option needs nothing, because tapping outside closes it.
  3. Keep the grabber as the visible cue. It is the iOS signal that a sheet can be swiped away. For VoiceOver, it gets a "Close" action, the way the Android handle already works for TalkBack.
